findings.finding: Landing analysis benefits from distinguishing contact, landed state and disarming, and inspecting synchronized time-series alongside the recorded trajectory.
findings.relevance: AL-022's landing-window errors include predictor drift after the thrust request becomes zero
findings.direction_alignment: Improve physics-based controller evaluation through ten coherent diagnosis and demonstration tools
findings.opportunity_or_risk: Phase separation prevents conflating motor-off drift with active control error, but does not establish causality or change acceptance
findings.engineering_cost: One bounded analysis exporter and a strict browser workspace over 24 retained recordings
findings.roadmap_delta: AL-023 provides a ten-feature flight diagnosis workspace before another controller correction
findings.verification_needed: Reconstruct retained recordings, independently audit phase arithmetic, preserve failures, inspect every real case and validate CSV and 3D

overall_recommendation: Expose contact and motor-off state alongside every physics sample before changing landing control.
evidence_gaps: No new flights or unseen cohort
State separation is descriptive and not causal
Synthetic sensors, ideal attitude/contact supervision and AL-010 yaw refinement remain limitations
